payload.source_label: Equation (1.5): p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/rho) p_x = 0

contract.statement: In the inherited real, one-dimensional, time-dependent setting, acoustic waves traveling in both directions are modeled by two unknown scalar fields: pressure perturbation p and particle velocity u. With constant bulk modulus K and density ρ, they satisfy p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/ρ) p_x = 0 simultaneously. Equivalently, q = (p,u)^T satisfies q_t + A q_x = 0 for A = [[0,K],[1/ρ,0]] [raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, (1.1) and its conventions; raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, (1.5), its explanatory paragraph, and (1.6)]. The selected passage leaves regularity and explicit parameter inequalities unstated [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, (1.5) and surrounding text].
assumptions: The modeling setting is acoustic waves propagating in both directions along a one-dimensional medium [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, paragraph preceding (1.5)].
The material coefficients K and ρ are constant rather than functions of position or time [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, paragraph following (1.5), 'constants K ... and ρ'].

The displayed partial derivatives must be meaningful for a classical reading of the equations; this is an analyst inference from the derivative notation, and the source supplies no explicit regularity class [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, (1.5); derivative convention on raw PDF page 23, printed page 1].

The selected passage states governing equations for unknown fields; it does not assert that every pair of functions satisfies those equations [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, introduction to (1.5) and 'These are the unknown functions to be determined'].

The inherited mathematical setting is a homogeneous, first-order, constant-coefficient linear system over the reals [raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, (1.1) and surrounding paragraphs; specialization in raw PDF page 24, (1.6)].

The source refers to Chapter 2 for derivation without reproducing it in this passage; no additional derivational hypotheses are extracted from that uninspected chapter [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, sentence preceding (1.5)].

The subsequent characteristic-variable discussion supplies the bidirectional interpretation using c = sqrt(K/ρ), w^1 = p + ρcu and w^2 = p − ρcu [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, discussion following (1.6)].
quantifiers: x and t are real independent variables denoting position in one spatial dimension and time, inherited from the setting of (1.1) [raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, introduction to and paragraph following (1.1)].

p and u are real scalar unknown functions of (x,t), forming the two components of q in that order [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, paragraph following (1.5) and (1.6); real-valued setting inherited from raw PDF page 23, paragraph following (1.1)].
K and ρ are fixed material constants, denoting bulk modulus of compressibility and density respectively [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, paragraph following (1.5)].
